summary.text: 慢 joins the heart-side form 忄, marking a disposition-related category, with 曼 as a phonetic element. Historical textual uses include laziness or neglect and slow movement; the evidence does not establish their order or link “slow” to 曼’s “long, extended” sense.

formation.text: 慢 is phonosemantic: 心, written in its conventional side form 忄, contributes a category associated with disposition or conduct, while 曼 supplies a sound cue. 曼 also has the meaning “long, extended,” but the evidence does not establish that this meaning gave rise to 慢 “slow.”

components.text: 忄 is the conventional side form of 心. In 慢 it contributes a heart-related semantic category associated with disposition or conduct; it is not a later replacement.
曼 is identified as the phonetic element in 慢. Uncertainty about 曼’s own ancient graphic interpretation is separate from this compound analysis.

sound_limitation.text: The cited phonetic analysis and Middle Chinese comparison support the conventional role, but do not settle the precise Old Chinese correspondence.

sound.text: In Middle Chinese categories, 慢 and 曼 share an 明 initial and departing tone, although their rhyme divisions differ. This comparison is compatible with the phonetic analysis without establishing its exact ancient correspondence.

history.text: The cited character inventory lists one small-seal form and one later form, but does not establish a sequence of graphic changes. It lists no oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript examples; this inventory does not prove earlier forms never existed.

uncertainties.text: The phonetic analysis of 曼 is conventional, but the precise Old Chinese sound correspondence remains unresolved. The cited Middle Chinese forms share an initial and departing tone, though their rhyme divisions differ.
The recorded slow-moving and laziness or neglect senses have no established relative chronology. The evidence does not show that “slow” developed from 曼’s “long, extended” meaning.

senses.text: 慢 is glossed as laziness or neglect. The cited examples do not establish that this sense preceded other recorded senses.

senses.period: received Shijing use; manuscript dating unresolved
senses.text: In the received Shijing phrase 叔馬慢忌, 慢 describes horses moving slowly near the end of a hunt. This textual use does not date when the sense first arose.
Current glosses include “leisurely” and “sluggish,” alongside “slow.” The evidence does not establish a dated path linking these meanings with one another or with laziness and neglect.
Textual uses are glossed as disrespect, arrogance, and treating lightly. Their dates and relationships to the other senses are unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited uses establish several meanings but not their order or a semantic path between them. The proposed link between 曼 “long, extended” and 慢 “slow” is not demonstrated.

overview.text: 慢 combines the heart-side form 忄, associated with disposition or conduct, with 曼 as a sound element. Recorded uses include “slow,” “laziness,” and “neglect”; the evidence does not link “slow” to 曼’s meaning “long, extended.”

components.text: The heart-side form marks a category associated with disposition or conduct.
曼 supplies a sound cue; its ancient graphic interpretation is disputed.

relationships.text: In 慢, 忄 is the side form of 心 and marks a heart-related semantic category associated with disposition or conduct.

曼 is the phonetic element in 慢. The Middle Chinese forms 慢 謨晏切 and 曼 無販切 share an 明 initial and departing tone, though their rhyme divisions differ. This supports the conventional analysis but does not settle the precise Old Chinese correspondence.
